newsitem.title: USA: Opposition to tobacco settlement mounting - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Opposition to tobacco settlement mounting - WSJ.

text.p: Opposition is building in settlement talks between state attorneys general and the tobacco industry over the issue of future liability, the Wall Street Journal reported.

In Thursday's electronic edition, the Journal said three of the 29 attorneys general who have sued tobacco companies to recoup health-care costs associated with ill smokers have expressed misgivings about the proposed settlement plan.
In particular, the attorneys general in Iowa, Maryland and Wisconsin, said they want to remove any proposal to limit an individual's right to sue the industry from the bargaining table.

"I'll be very reluctant to agree to any significant limitations on individual liability," Iowa Attorney General Tom Miller said. "It's hard to give special liability protection to the tobacco industry when they're the worst not the best and are only now doing what a responsible industry should have done 40 years ago."

Wisconsin Attorney General Jim Doyle said: "Even though we have no real authority, we are bargaining away the rights of future individuals. I am very uncomfortable in limiting citizens' rights to go to court."

Their criticisms came as Mississippi Attorney General Mike Moore said on Wednesday that he would know within the next eight to 10 days whether progress could be made on a host of remaining issues, including the industry's legal liability in future lawsuits. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610))
